title: Nai
summary: The pan flute of the Carpathian lands: a single curved raft of closed pipes of graduated length, played by moving the lips along the rims. Each pipe is one note; strike a pipe to blow across it.
howToPlay: The longest pipes are the lowest notes.
Strike a pipe to blow across its rim.
Follow the notes as they come to their pipes.
rules: One raft, one scale, from the longest pipe to the shortest.
Strike each pipe close to its beat.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The nai is played in village bands and by solo musicians, with a soft breathy tone and a rich vibrato.
